note: Adapted from the original description of the new species by Scheffrahn et al. 2025 (in English), original name Nasutitermes aurantius sp. nov., type locality Omar Torrijos Herrera National Park, Coclé Province, Panama; includes the diagnostic characters and the alate (only 2 males), soldier (n=10) and worker (two forms) with measurements. The original gives all measurements as 'mean (range)', copied here with the range joined by an em dash. In the original the major-worker head width is set as '1.04 X– (range 99–1.04)', evidently a dropped leading 0, noted in the text. The female alate is unknown.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among the Central American Nasutitermes species the soldier is unique in its small size and orange-yellow head capsule. Among the South American Nasutitermes species the soldier comes closest to Nasutitermes jaraguae (Holmgren, 1910) in size and colour, but the nasus is proportionally longer and more slender. The enteric valve (EVA) of the worker is unique among the Neotropical Nasutitermes: the distal cushion region is sclerotized, oval, granular and spinose. By head width the alate is the smallest of the Central American Nasutitermes species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Alate (female unknown): vertex dark brown, genae paler; densely hairy with hairs of various lengths. Fontanelle a narrow slit. Eyes nearly circular, prominent by almost half their diameter. Ocelli transparent, more than one diameter from the eye margin. Pronotum concolorous with the head; anterior margin straight, posterior margin slightly concave; pilosity as on the head. Antennae 15-segmented, segment-order formula 2>3<4=5, segment 3 narrowest. Measurements (mm, n=2, males): head length (to the end of the clypeus) 1.23, 1.28; maximum head width (with eyes) 1.21, 1.25; maximum eye diameter 0.31, 0.35; maximum ocellus diameter 0.10, 0.11; maximum pronotum length 0.56, 0.59; maximum pronotum width 0.94, 0.95; right fore wing length from the wing suture 9.37, 9.94; body length with wings 11.36, 11.64.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier (monomorphic): head orange-yellow with a brownish tinge, nasus darker. Head nearly triangular in dorsal view, the sides narrowing rather steeply towards the nasus; slightly constricted behind the antennal sockets. In lateral view the head is slightly convex above and behind the antennal sockets. Four long bristles near the top of the vertex elevation and 2 long bristles near the posterior 1/3 of the vertex. Nasus narrowly conical, with distinct bristles at the tip; the nasus is almost parallel with the ventral margin of the head. Antennae 13-segmented, segment-order formula 2<3>4<5. Mandibles with a distinct pointed process. Pronotum with shallow lobes forming a 120° angle; the margins of the dorsal lobe with several long bristles and many very short bristles. Posterior margins of the abdominal tergites with several long bristles, the interior with many short bristles. Postmentum about 1/4 of the total head height, in lateral view forming a shallow convexity opposite the vertex depression. Measurements (mm, n=10, range in parentheses): head length 1.53 (1.46—1.58); head length (to the base of the nasus) 0.91 (0.86—0.94); nasus length 0.62 (0.57—0.67); maximum head width 0.84 (0.77—0.89); pronotum width 0.44 (0.40—0.49); hind tibia length 0.86 (0.86—0.91).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker (two forms): head capsule pale yellow or pale orange; about 80 bristles of various lengths. Vertex with a depression behind the clypeus; postclypeus small, its posterior margin steep in lateral view. Fontanelle transparent, large, oval; the brain prominent and white, with an incision cut by the fontanelle. Major worker with 14 antennal segments, minor worker with 13; the segment-order formula in both is 2>3<4=5. The mandibular dentition (wood-feeding type) and the gap between the 3rd marginal tooth and the molar prominence are similar in the two forms; the cutting edge of the left mandible is straight; the molar plate has ridges. The midgut develops into a complete ring from the crop to P1; P1 is long, tubular in dorsal view, S-shaped from M to the EVA, its attachment visible through the cuticle. The enteric valve consists of 3 cushion regions, each with about 80—100 circular scales in the anterior part, each scale with a small posteriorly directed point; the posterior part of each cushion region is sclerotized and oval, each formed of about 10—12 polygons, of which the central 4—5 polygons are granular and each bears a spine; a few scales are scattered between and in front of the cushion regions. Head width (mm, n=10 per form): major worker 1.04 (set as '99—1.04' in the original, which from the context should be 0.99—1.04); minor worker 0.87 (0.84—0.91).
